newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH FOREIGN MINISTER BACKS ROMANIA NATO BID.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH FOREIGN MINISTER BACKS ROMANIA NATO BID.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Wednesday that Romania should be part of the first wave of NATO enlargement to former East Bloc countries in 1999.

"France will back Romania's candidacy," de Charette told reporters. "France believes that Romania should be among the countries starting negotiations" at the military alliance's Madrid summit in July, he said.
Countries usually included in the first wave are Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungaria, but de Charette said the list was not formally defined.
European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier, on a visit to Bucharest on Tuesday, already said Romania should be among the new NATO members.
Romania's geographic location and political stability were assets which qualified the Balkan country to join NATO, he said.
French President Jacques Chirac is due to visit Romania on February 20-22.
